newsitem.title: INDIA: Demand resistance caps Indian sugar rally.
newsitem.headline: Demand resistance caps Indian sugar rally.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Monday lost some of its recent gains as demand resistance from consumers capped a rally while profit-taking by millers and local stockists dragged prices down, dealers said.
In the ready delivery sugar, S-30 fell by 15 rupees at 1,400/1,435 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 moved down by 5/20 rupees at 1,440/1,500 rupees per quintal.
"Improved arrivals from mills to the market as well as fears that the Indian government may release more free sale sugar also subdued market sentiments," one broker said.
The government last week raised the free sale quota for the current month by 50,000 tonnes to 800,000 tonnes and dealers said they expect the government to increase this.
The free sale quota for last month was 700,000 tonnes.
Sugar mill delivery dropped to 1,325/1,345 rupees per quintal from 1,350/1,370 rupees as outstation buying eased at the mill level.
Slow offtake by outstation buyers at the mill level have increased arrivals of sugar from mills to the local market and sentiments remained subdued at the close of the session.
